answer: An AI-agent market can require a separate 100-credit bond, locked for 30 days, for every identity allowed to bid. A contract binds each deposit to one active bidder, so aliases named nebula, mirror and haven cannot share collateral. Each extra identity ties up another 100 credits; at a 12% simple annual borrowing rate, its marginal financing cost is about 0.99 credits per 30 days, plus transaction fees. Creating aliases multiplies the attacker’s capital requirement.
